task_name: Ember and Oak - Restaurant launch reel system
client_brief:
We are opening the second room at Ember and Oak and we need a launch package that makes people hungry before they read a word. Everything the shoot left us is short and silent, five second takes off the pass and around the room, so treat this as a short form set rather than a film with a story to tell. The food leads: each film opens on a shot of food, and the cut shows real char, visible texture and a room that feels alive. The message rides on type, not on a voice.

Please cut a 12 to 15 second launch reel in 16:9, built from at least five different takes, then an 8 to 10 second upright cutdown from at least four different takes and a 6 to 8 second square bumper from at least three, each standing on its own rather than reading as a crop of the wide one. The upright keeps all type and the mark clear of the top 250 and bottom 320 pixels. Every film stays silent by our own choice, so the words have to carry it on screen. Each film ends on its own closing card carrying the mark, the line “Second room now open” and the booking action “Book a table”, designed as a card. Please do not drop the mark over the last available frame and call that an ending. The square bumper calls out one dish from emberoak_menu_callouts.txt, with its price on the line beneath the name. In every film, any dish name, price or allergen line is taken word for word from emberoak_menu_callouts.txt.

One correction to the manifest: emberoak_pass_call.mov has no audio despite the name. Treat it as b roll like the rest.

The reel cover, the window poster and the three dish callout cards are being handled separately, so this delivery is the three films only.

brand_identity.tagline: What fire does to good meat.
brand_identity.sector: Food and beverage: a wood fired neighbourhood grill serving walk-in trade and delivery, opening a second room.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: A single-room wood fired grill on the west side of Providence, Rhode Island, opening its second room in launch week, run by a small owner-operator team.
brand_identity.about: Ember and Oak is a wood fired grill on the west side of Providence, one hearth you can see from every table, mains around thirty four dollars. Launch week opens the second room. The brand is fire, char and appetite: warm, loud and alive, built to make somebody hungry in the first two seconds.
brand_identity.audience: Walk-in diners on the west side deciding in the time it takes to scroll past, plus delivery orders. Neighbourhood people who want a room that feels alive, not a tasting menu and not a value grill.
brand_identity.price_positioning: A casual premium wood fired grill, mains around thirty four dollars. The grade runs warm, the cut is fast, the food fills the frame and the type is bold and immediate. Never moody fine dining, never a discount grill with a deal burned across the frame.

brand_identity.typography: Ember and Oak runs on two faces. Dish names set in Red Hat Display Black capitals at 112 px on 120 px leading, tracked minus 0.020 em, always over two lines, with a 12 px Ember Orange bar burning behind the baseline of the lower line and stopping flush with its final letter. Under it the price and room line sets in Atlas Grotesk Bold at 56 px on 62 px, tracked minus 0.010 em. Descriptions set in Atlas Grotesk Regular at 34 px on 44 px with tracking at zero and no more than 65 characters a line, and fine print such as hours and delivery sets in Atlas Grotesk Regular at 22 px on 30 px, tracked plus 0.030 em. Printed menus and window cards hold the same relationship at 34 pt names and 10 pt body on 14 pt. A dish name is never set in lowercase.
brand_identity.voice: Warm, direct, hungry. Short lines with heat in them. Example line the brand would write: 'The chop, the char, the fire you can see from your table. Second room now open.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: The mark survives only as a small raster: a two word lockup inside a thin ring, sitting on a cream square baked into the picture rather than behind it. It has to be recovered as clean, placeable artwork before it can go on the end card or the window poster.
brand_identity.values: Appetite and honesty: show the real food from the real service, and make the room feel like what it is. The reel should read like the room smells.
brand_identity.signature_type_move: Every dish name sets in Red Hat Display Black capitals over two lines with a twelve px Ember Orange bar burning behind the baseline of the lower line and stopping flush with its final letter, so the name always looks like it is resting on something hot.

type_system.signature_move: The hot bar. Every dish name sets in Red Hat Display Black capitals over two lines at 112 px on 120 px, tracked minus 0.020 em, with a 12 px Ember Orange bar burning behind the baseline of the lower line and stopping flush with its final letter, so the name always looks like it is resting on something hot. That bar is the first thing a viewer sees.
rules: Never set a dish name in lowercase.
Every dish name breaks over two lines; the Ember Orange bar sits behind the baseline of the lower line only and stops flush with its last letter, never running past it.
The bar is 12 px deep at the 112 px screen size and scales with the name, never with the frame.
Dish names always track minus 0.020 em; no other step may borrow that tracking.
In print, dish names set 34 pt and body 10 pt on 14 pt.
Never let the type go moody fine dining, and never burn a discount deal across the frame.

palette_rules.distribution: Grounds and panels are Charcoal, Flame Yellow or Cream, and every closing card has one of them as a solid ground. Type and the mark are Cream on Charcoal and Charcoal on Flame Yellow, as type_system step 02 sets, and Charcoal on Cream, as emberoak_mark.png sets the mark; type set directly on footage is Cream. A price or room line sits only on a solid Charcoal or Flame Yellow panel (type_system step 02), never on Cream or directly on footage. Ember Orange is the hot bar behind every dish name and is never type, a ground or a panel. Beyond the hot bars, Ember Orange, Oak Brown and Char Red are accents for thin rules and dividers only, together no more than 5% of the designed, non-footage area.
palette_rules.opacity: Every palette colour is used solid, at 100% opacity. No tint, transparency, gradient, glow, shadow, outline or blend mode is applied to any palette colour, type, bar or the mark, and no scrim, vignette, gradient or overlay of any colour, black and white included, is laid over footage or a still: type that needs separation from the footage sits on a solid panel in the colours the distribution rule sets. A colour grade applied to the footage itself is not an overlay. Cuts and dissolves between shots are transitions, not tints; colour and opacity are judged on a settled frame.
palette_rules.forbidden: No colour outside the six palette hexes for type, bars, panels, rules, buttons or icons, and no discount or deal flash, badge or burst in any colour, which the type rules forbid.
palette_rules.photography: Footage and stills keep their own colour under the warm grade the brand positioning sets. A warm colour grade is allowed; a flat palette-colour overlay, tint or duotone that replaces their own colours is not. No detail is painted, generated or extended into footage or stills.
